units.translation: a corrupt gloss of Hesychius, with which Schmidt compared the same author's gloss ἀτυζηλόν [fearful, unseen, obscure] (codex ἀττύζηλον): φοβερὸν, ἀφανὲς, ἄσημον [fearful, unseen, obscure].
Itys, son of Tereus and Procne.
and through all time my heart feeds on groans

where the first syllable is to be pronounced short, as in Arist. Lys. 1110, but it is long in Theocritus in the refrain beginning with ἴυγξ [magic wheel] of Idyll 2. In Aeschylus the scholiast explains φίλιον [loving] rather inaccurately: see Thes. vol. 4 p. 725.
you remind me of my good companions with a magic wheel
ἴυζε καὶ βόα [cry aloud and shout]. Hermann noted that these words are repeated from earlier.
and he cried aloud a voice
Iphigenia was the title of a play by Aeschylus (fr. 91, 92).

where for metrical reasons I wrote Ιφιγενείαν [Iphigenia] with changed accent, just as εὐκλεία [good repute] and ἀνοία [folly] are sometimes found for εὔκλεια [good repute] and ἄνοια [folly], and other such forms.
but Iphigenia will lovingly welcome him
a suspect word in a corrupt passage, Suppl. 850

where the scholiast says ἴχαρ [desire] means τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν [the desire], τὴν ἄτην τῆς φρενός [the infatuation of the mind]. Similarly grammarians explain ἰχανᾶν [to desire] by ἐπιθυμεῖν [to desire] and γλίχεσθαι [to long for], on which see Hermann's note vol. 2 p. 43. A similar word is found in Theognostus in Cramer's Anecd. Oxon. vol. 2 p. 80, 10: 'neuter disyllables ending in -αρ with ι in the penult are two, πῖαρ [fat] and ἶχαρ [desire]' (codex πίαρ καὶ ἴλαρ [fat and cheerful]), which Lobeck in Paralip. p. 205 suggested could be ἴχαρ [desire], but later in Ῥηματικῷ ρ. 313 he considered λίχαρ [greedy] or γλίχαρ [greedy] because of the scholiast's interpretation ἐπιθυμίαν [desire].
I bid you to let go of force and the infatuation of your mind
the desire, the infatuation of the mind
neuter disyllables ending in -αρ with ι in the penult are two, πῖαρ [fat] and ἶχαρ [desire]
which the scholiast explains as τῇ τοὺς ἰχθῦς τιτρωσκούση τριαίνῃ [the trident that wounds the fish].
the trident that wounds the fish
like tunas or some catch of fish
I surround with a vast net, as for fish
coming to the same track of my former words
having landed on the invisible track of the wandering
and they returned to the old track
I will not turn aside from my former track of mind
and tracking in my own paths
before the old pain ceases, new ichor
